Article Title: ‘Key growth engine for the world’: IMF hails India’s 7.8% growth, backs GDP estimate changes
Article Text:
IMF hails India’s 7.8% growth, calls economy a key global growth engine

IMF backs changes to GDP estimates

GDP figures face questions

India’s economy has stayed on the growth track despite the energy price shock, with real GDP rising 7.8% in the April-June quarter. The IMF hailed the stronger-than-expected performance, saying that the growth was boosted by better-than-expected activity in services and exports.At a press briefing, IMF spokesperson Julie Kozack said, “India's real GDP in the second quarter grew by 7.8 per cent. That was above our staff's expectations and also the consensus among other observers. This upward surprise was driven by stronger-than-expected activity in the services sector and in exports.”“The outturn also underscores the resilience of the Indian economy despite the energy price shock. It also means that India does remain a key growth engine for the world,” she added.The 7.8% growth in real GDP for Q1 FY27, covering April-June, was higher than the Reserve Bank of India’s earlier estimate of 7%. Data from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) showed real GDP at Rs 81.36 lakh crore in the quarter, compared with Rs 75.46 lakh crore in the same period of FY26.Alongside its positive assessment of India’s growth, the IMF also welcomed changes made to the country’s GDP estimation system.Kozack said the latest GDP release included a new index of industrial production and a new producer price index series. According to her, both should help improve India’s GDP estimates.“I can say that the latest GDP release, the one that we just talked about for Q2, it incorporated both a new index of industrial production. It also included a new producer price index series, and those two new series should help improve India's GDP estimates,” Kozack said.She said the IMF welcomed India’s efforts to modernise its macroeconomic statistics and encouraged the authorities to keep strengthening the statistical framework and data quality.“And we welcome these important steps that India is taking to modernise its macroeconomic statistics. And of course, we encourage the authorities to continue to further strengthen the statistical framework and data quality along the lines that they're progressing,” she said.The IMF’s comments come amid a debate over India’s latest GDP numbers and the revisions behind them. Former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg had questioned the reported 7.8% growth in the April-June quarter, pointing to a revision in the previous year’s current GDP from Rs 86 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore.Garg had said that without the revision, growth at current prices would have been around 2.6%, adding to questions over India’s GDP calculations.The IMF also said the latest numbers showed the resilience of India’s economy. It welcomed the changes to the GDP estimation system, noting that the new industrial production index and producer price index series would help improve GDP estimates.
Article Summary: IMF hails India’s 7.8% growth, calls economy a key global growth engine. IMF also welcomed changes made to the country's GDP estimation system. Former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg had questioned the reported 7.7% growth.

Article Title: Rupee tumbles 27 paise against US dollar as crude prices hold firm above $108 per barrel
Article Text:
Rupee falls 27 paise against US dollar

Rupee began Friday on a weak note, falling 27 paise to extend its decline against the US dollar. In early trading, the currency touched 95.79 as high crude oil prices and foreign portfolio outflows continued to weigh it down.Rupee began the session at 95.70 against the dollar at the interbank foreign exchange market before weakening to 95.79. This marked a 27-paise fall from its previous close. Earlier on Thursday, the currency had already lost 44 paise, ending the session at 95.52.According to forex traders, the currency is facing pressure even as India has several factors supporting it. Record foreign exchange reserves, active intervention by the Reserve Bank and robust domestic growth are providing support, but rising global yields and crude prices above $108 are adding to pressure on the country's import bill."For the rupee, the pressure continues. It remains in an uptrend beyond 95 on the back of costly oil and foreign portfolio outflows, and we could see 96, with 95 now acting as support," said Anindya Banerjee, head of commodity and currency research, Kotak Securities.Banerjee said rupee's supporting factors include record foreign exchange reserves, the Reserve Bank's active presence in the market and domestic growth of 7.8 per cent.However, he said the import bill is likely to remain the dominant force in the near term with crude above $100 and global yields rising.Investors are now expected to watch US and Indian inflation data for further direction.The dollar index was at 99.16, up 0.12 per cent. The index measures the strength of the US currency against a basket of six currencies.In the oil market, Brent crude futures were trading 0.76 per cent lower at $108.45 per barrel. The benchmark remained at elevated levels amid escalating US-Iran tensions and concerns over disruption to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz.Pressure was also visible in the domestic stock market. Sensex fell 628.24 points to 74,257.69 in early trade, while Nifty declined 221.20 points to 23,255.10.Foreign Institutional Investors also remained sellers in the equity market. They offloaded shares worth Rs 438.24 crore on a net basis on Thursday, according to exchange data.
Article Summary: Rupee began Friday on a weak note, falling 27 paise to extend its decline against the US dollar. In early trading, the currency touched 95.79 as high crude oil prices and foreign portfolio outflows continued to weigh down. Record foreign exchange reserves, active intervention by the Reserve Bank and robust domestic growth are providing support.

Article Title: IRCTC records highest-ever 20.06 lakh ticket bookings in a day; system capacity doubled as festive rush drives demand, 19.51 lakh more booked next day
Article Text:
Indian Railways is undertaking several measures to modernise and strengthen its rail ticket booking system.

IRCTC sets 20 lakh ticket booking record

IRCTC modernizes train ticket booking website

NGeT refresh

New user interface

System measures: CDN and Anti-BOT

Restrictions during the opening booking window

Action against misuse

The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) has set a new ticket booking record! Online booking of train tickets now accounts for 89% of total train ticket bookings on the Indian Railways network and this rush became evident when the festive season train ticket advance reservation window began.Indian Railways has recently reduced the advanced reservation window from 120 days to 60 days. With Diwali 2026 on 8th November 2026 this year, the 60 day period advance booking began this week.According to IRCTC, its website handled a huge rush on September 7, 2026. The ticket booking website registered its highest-ever single-day booking, with 20,06,353 tickets booked. The record was achieved amid festive-season ARP booking.The system continued to handle the heavy booking load the following day as well, with 19,50,699 tickets booked on September 8, 2026, IRCTC said. This further demonstrated the capacity of the NGet robust booking system to manage large volumes of transactions, it claimed.The current booking pattern shows that only 8.43% to 14.14% of the day's total bookings take place during the first hour, between 8:00 am and 9:00 am.More than 85% of bookings are successfully completed later in the day.The first 15 minutes, from 8:00 am to 8:15 am, consistently see the largest booking volume, indicating the period of peak concurrent demand.During the festive season last year, the highest single-day booking stood at 18,40,203 tickets.Indian Railways is undertaking several measures to modernise and strengthen its rail ticket booking system, including the rollout of a new UI beta version from July 15, 2026.Online booking now accounts for around 89% of all reserved tickets. The continued system upgrades have also enabled IRCTC to handle exceptionally high booking volumes during the festive season, it says.IRCTC said that the record booking performance has been made possible by several important measures:A comparison of the server infrastructure before and after the NGeT refresh shows a substantial increase in capacity. The overall capacity of the ecosystem has been raised to approximately twice its earlier level by replacing the old servers with new ones.The increase has not been limited to hardware. Software optimisation and architectural improvements have also contributed to a substantial, manifold expansion in capacity compared with the earlier system.IRCTC introduced the beta version of its new User Interface with effect from July 15, 2026. The redesigned interface has a contemporary appearance influenced by global design trends such as Glassmorphism, creating a more visually engaging experience from the login stage through ticket confirmation, IRCTC said.The new interface also aims to present booking information in a more organised and accessible manner. One of the key changes is that availability across different travel classes, including Sleeper, AC 3 Tier and AC 2 Tier, is displayed together on a single screen.This allows passengers to compare available options without repeatedly navigating between screens, making it easier to assess the choices and complete the booking process.IRCTC has partnered with a leading technology player to deploy Anti-BOT and CDN capabilities. Anti-BOT measures have helped reduce malicious BOT traffic by 55% to 65% in recent months.The Content Delivery Network (CDN), meanwhile, is being used to serve static content and has reduced the load on the NGeT (Next Generation e-Ticketing) system. This has helped improve the experience for genuine and verified users.IRCTC's Network Security Team is also taking action against fake websites and mobile applications that impersonate the organisation.Authorised ticketing agents across categories, including YTSKs, RTSAs and IRCTC Agents, are not permitted to book ARP tickets during the first 10 minutes of the booking window, from 08:00 AM to 08:10 AM.Since October 12, 2025, only Aadhaar-authenticated users have been allowed to book tickets during the opening ARP window.On each ARP opening day, the NGeT system has successfully handled between 1.33 crore and 1.74 crore logins and processed 17 lakh to 20 lakh bookings, reflecting its increased capacity to manage periods of intense demand.Continuous action has also been taken against misuse of the ticketing system. As part of these measures, 3.04 crore User IDs have been deactivated and 6.33 crore IDs have been placed under revalidation. In addition, 16,041 suspicious email domains have been blocked and 592 complaints have been filed on the Cyber Crime Portal covering 4.21 lakh suspicious PNRs.
Article Summary: Indian Railways is undertaking several measures to modernise and strengthen its rail ticket booking system. Online booking now accounts for around 89% of all reserved tickets. The system upgrades have also enabled IRCTC to handle exceptionally high booking volumes during the festive season, it says.

Article Title: US diesel prices at record $6: American farmers feel the heat as harvest season begins
Article Text:
US diesel prices soar past $6 a gallon

US farmers are facing a bigger fuel bill as diesel prices hit record highs just as the corn and soybean harvest gets underway, pushing up the cost of running combines, tractors and trucks.The national average price of diesel reached $5.85 a gallon on September 4, the first time it had risen that high, and climbed further to $6.05 a gallon on Friday, according to AAA. That is 60% higher than the roughly $3.76 a gallon average recorded before the US and Israel launched their war against Iran in late February.The rise has added to a difficult year for farmers already paying more for fertiliser, seeds, equipment, chemicals and other inputs. The higher fuel costs are also affecting the movement of crops, from fields to farms and eventually to buyers.“Those prices hurt," Paul Mitchell, a professor of agricultural and applied economics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison told AP. “And it’s not just the harvesting. It’s the hauling of everything, moving the grain or the silage from the field to the farm and then from the farm to wherever they're selling it.”For farmers, diesel is difficult to avoid during harvest. Jason Kurtz, who grows corn and soybeans near Forest City, Missouri, said his fuel bill had doubled this year. His combine alone burns about 200 gallons (760 litres) of diesel each day, and he expects to operate it for 30 days. He also needs fuel for a tractor and trucks.“We have to harvest," Kurtz said in an interview at his farm about 90 miles (145 kilometres) outside Kansas City on Tuesday. “We have to run the machines. We have to use the diesel, so it cuts into our bottom line.”Kurtz, 49, said his finances were “already tight” after having to spend more on fertiliser and chemicals this year.The surge in diesel prices has followed a jump in crude oil costs, with disruptions to tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz during the war affecting fuel supplies. Crude oil is the main ingredient in both diesel and petrol.The higher costs are putting particular pressure on farms that have less financial room to absorb another increase in expenses.“Farms that are cash strapped, they’re the ones that are most having to figure out what to cut to make this work," Mitchell said. “There are a lot of farms facing that.”Kurtz, who voted for US President Donald Trump, said he planned to postpone some farm work in the hope that diesel prices would ease later.
Article Summary: The national average price of diesel reached $5.85 a gallon on September 4. That is 60% higher than the roughly $3.76 a gallon average recorded before the US and Israel launched their war against Iran in late February. The higher fuel costs are also affecting the movement of crops, from fields to farms and eventually to buyers.

Article Title: Report: MSMEs need digital infra
Article Text:
NPCI Bharat BillPay

MUMBAI: NPCI Bharat BillPay has proposed a centralised digital infrastructure to connect invoices, payments, reconciliation and financing, to fix the biggest constraints faced by MSMEs - the difficulty of turning sales into cash and cash flows into credit. The system could help address the MSME sector's Rs 60 lakh crore formal credit gap, while reducing the friction involved in collecting and matching payments.The proposed infrastructure would digitise the order-to-cash cycle through standardised APIs and automate reconciliation across more than 20 crore monthly GST e-invoices. Buyer-confirmed invoices could become financeable records, allowing lenders to assess borrowers on the strength of their cash flows rather than relying only on collateral. A common information layer could also reduce the mismatches that contribute to delays in MSME receivables.According to a report by NPCI Bharat BillPay and Bain & Company, formal credit of around Rs 34 lakh crore meets only part of an estimated Rs 92 lakh crore demand for MSME debt, leaving a gap of around Rs 60 lakh crore. The shortage is greatest among smaller enterprises, where formal channels meet only 30% to 40% of debt demand.
Article Summary: NPCI Bharat BillPay has proposed a centralised digital infrastructure to connect invoices, payments, reconciliation and financing. The system could help address the MSME sector's Rs 60 lakh crore formal credit gap, while reducing the friction involved in collecting and matching payments.

Article Title: Two homebuyers booked flats and paid Rs 1.16 crore in 2013, they were promised possession by 2014; years later they still had no homes, MahaRERA orders builder to refund money with interest
Article Text:
The two homebuyers received an allotment letter dated February 18, 2013. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did MahaRERA rule in favour of the homebuyers?

Homebuyers to receive refund with interest

Why property buyers should maintain a payment trail

What to check before booking a property

Two homebuyers booked flats on the sixth and seventh floors of a Mumbai housing project in 2013. They were assured that they would get possession for the flats by December 2014. But their dream of getting the flats remains elusive.The buyers claimed to have collectively paid Rs 1.16 crore for Flat Nos. 603 and 703 and subsequently approached MahaRERA seeking a refund, along with compensation of Rs 20 lakh each.The Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority has directed the developer to refund the amounts paid, along with applicable interest, after noting that the project remained incomplete and its registration had lapsed without an extension.The two homebuyers received an allotment letter dated February 18, 2013. According to their complaint, the developer told them that construction up to the fifth floor was complete and that the sixth and seventh floors would be completed by 2014.One homebuyer said he paid Rs 50 lakh by cheque and Rs 6 lakh in cash for Flat No. 603. The other claimed to have paid Rs 50 lakh by cheque and Rs 10 lakh in cash for Flat No. 703. The developer acknowledged receiving the Rs 50 lakh cheque payments from both buyers.The payments were completed during 2013-14, after which the buyers repeatedly sought possession. They said the developer continued to tell them that approvals required for construction above the fifth floor had not yet been obtained.The buyers pointed out that the Commencement Certificate dated October 22, 2010, permitted construction only up to the fifth floor. Despite this, they said the developer sold the sixth- and seventh-floor flats during 2012-13, assuring them that the additional approvals would be secured and the project completed by 2014.They also relied on architect certificates dated July 29, 2017, and March 13, 2019, which showed no progress in construction of the upper floors.The developer, however, maintained that the buyers knew about the pending approvals when they booked the flats. It attributed the delay to disputes concerning municipal charges, the COVID-19 pandemic and the lockdown, according to an ET report.The developer described the complaint as forum shopping and disputed the amounts claimed.For Flat No. 603, it said only Rs 45,24,000 had been received and denied the additional Rs 10.76 lakh claimed by one homebuyer. For Flat No. 703, it acknowledged receiving Rs 50 lakh but said Rs 10 lakh had subsequently been refunded, leaving Rs 40 lakh.MahaRERA found that substantial amounts had been paid for both flats and that the project had lapsed on its portal without the developer seeking an extension.“The latest architect certificate dated 31.02.2019 uploaded on the portal substantiates that the project remains incomplete and the respondent thereafter has failed to update the progress of the project, which substantiated that the project remains incomplete and are at default,” the tribunal said according to ET.The developer had also failed to hand over possession with the requisite Occupation Certificate within the stipulated period.Rishabh Gandhi, Former Judge and Founder, Rishabh Gandhi and Advocates, told ET that the prolonged and continuing default was decisive.He said the combination of the lapsed project, incomplete construction, absence of an Occupation Certificate and the fact that the allotted flats were above the fifth floor strengthened the buyers' case.Gandhi pointed to Section 18 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. “Where the promoter fails to complete the project or give possession, an allottee who chooses to withdraw is entitled to refund with prescribed interest. MahaRERA rightly emphasised that a homebuyer cannot be made to wait indefinitely for the promoter to obtain approvals and complete the project.”The buyers also had allotment letters, payment records and legal notices dated 14.09.2020 formally recording their withdrawal. The MahaRERA portal showed that the project registration had lapsed.MahaRERA has directed the developer to refund the amounts established as having been paid towards the respective flats, together with applicable interest calculated from the respective payment dates. The developer has 60 days from the order to make the payment.It must also pay Rs 20,000 each to both the homebuyers as costs.The homebuyers claimed payments of Rs 56 lakh and Rs 60 lakh, respectively. However, the figures included cash payments of Rs 6 lakh and Rs 10 lakh, which were disputed.Gandhi said the order should therefore not be interpreted as automatically awarding Rs 56 lakh to Kutty and Rs 60 lakh. “MahaRERA has directed refund of the amounts paid towards the consideration of the respective flats, together with interest.”The final refund will depend on the amount that can ultimately be established as having been paid, particularly because the cash components were disputed.Cash payments do not automatically defeat a buyer's legal claim, but proving an undocumented payment can become difficult. Gandhi noted that both buyers claimed cash components without receipts, while the developer disputed those amounts.“ that problem is visible in this case: both purchasers alleged cash components – Rs 6 lakh and Rs 10 lakh - but there were no receipts for those payments, and the developer disputed the amounts.”A bank transfer, by comparison, creates a contemporaneous record of payment. Section 269ST of the Income-tax Act also restricts receipt of Rs 2 lakh or more in cash in the circumstances specified under the provision.A RERA registration number alone should not be the only check before buying a flat. Gandhi said buyers should examine the sanctioned plan, Commencement Certificate, approvals for the specific wing and floor, title and encumbrances, declared completion date, pending approvals and litigation, as well as quarterly project updates on the MahaRERA portal.
Article Summary: Two homebuyers booked flats on the sixth and seventh floors of a Mumbai housing project in 2013. They were assured that they would get possession for the flats by December 2014. The buyers claimed to have collectively paid Rs 1.16 crore for Flat Nos. 603 and 703. The Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority has directed the developer to refund the amounts paid, along with applicable interest.

Article Title: Nvidia weighs $10 billion investment in Anthropic’s mega IPO: Report
Article Text:
Anthropic plans massive IPO

Nvidia and Anthropic's growing ties

Amazon and Google are also major backers

From $965 billion to a possible $2 trillion

Anthropic is planning what could be the biggest IPO in history, with the artificial intelligence giant looking to raise as much as $100 billion at a valuation of around $2 trillion. Nvidia is in talks to become a major early investor in the offering, according to two people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters.Nvidia is considering putting up to $10 billion into the IPO, one of the people said. The talks are still going on and the plans could change, the sources said. They requested anonymity because the discussions are private.If the deal goes ahead, Nvidia would become an early investor in what could be the biggest IPO ever. Its involvement could also strengthen the close business relationship between Nvidia and Anthropic, one of the chipmaker's major customers.Nvidia's possible investment comes as Anthropic depends heavily on Nvidia's chips to run its AI models. At the same time, Anthropic is looking for other chip suppliers as rising demand for Claude has put pressure on its available computing capacity.Nvidia had already said in November 2025 that it would invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic as part of a wider partnership.Under the deal, Anthropic agreed to buy $30 billion of Microsoft Azure computing capacity powered by Nvidia chips.Anchor investors usually agree to buy a fixed amount of shares before an IPO is offered to the wider market. Their early investment can give other investors confidence in the listing.Large IPOs have increasingly looked for such early investors because of the huge amounts of money they are trying to raise. Nvidia and Amazon were among the anchor investors in chip designer Arm's IPO, while Saudi Arabia's PIF was among the anchor investors for SpaceX.Anthropic already has some of the world's biggest technology companies as investors. Amazon and Google are also among its major suppliers of computing power.In April, Anthropic said it would commit more than $100 billion over 10 years to Amazon's AWS while using more than 1 million of Amazon's Trainium2 chips. It has also agreed with Google and Broadcom to add several gigawatts of TPU capacity.The company is trying to get access to more computing power as its revenue has grown sharply. It is also building an in-house team to design its own chips for Claude, with the aim of having greater control over its hardware costs.The proposed IPO would mark another big jump in Anthropic's valuation.The Claude maker raised $65 billion in May at a post-money valuation of $965 billion. Its annualised revenue run rate had crossed $65 billion by the end of July, compared with about $9 billion at the end of 2025, according to the company.The possible $2 trillion valuation also depends partly on Anthropic's projections of around $190 billion to $200 billion in revenue in 2028, Reuters previously reported.The listing is expected to be completed before the US midterm elections in November.An Anthropic listing would add to a series of major IPOs that have helped push the US market towards a record year. Elon Musk's SpaceX made its debut in June.US IPOs, excluding special-purpose acquisition companies, raised a record $137 billion through the end of August, according to Dealogic.
Article Summary: Anthropic is planning what could be the biggest IPO in history. It is looking to raise as much as $100 billion at a valuation of around $2 trillion. Nvidia is in talks to become a major early investor in the offering.

Article Title: Ice cream to defence: How Canada’s tariff war with US is boosting local businesses
Article Text:
Canada’s tariff war with US is boosting local businesses

Local products in the basket

‘Buy Canadian’ gets a boost

Defence firms look beyond the US

Others face price pressure

The US and Canada are embroiled in a tariff war, and it may “will come at a cost” for Ottawa as the Canadian PM Mark Carney had warned. But the fight is proving a win for at rather unusual sectors: from the ice-cream counter and gift shops to wineries and even defence manufacturing.As American goods face fresh Canadian tariffs, local businesses have seen an uptick due to the “buy Canadian” wave.Prime Minister Mark Carney has warned that moving away from the US as Canada’s biggest trading partner “will come at a cost,” adding that the counter-tariffs on American goods “are necessary to protect our workers”.The new Canadian levies cover nearly C$28 billion ($20 billion) of American products, ranging from steel and furniture to cotton T-shirts, with tariffs as high as 50%.For Chapman’s, Canada’s largest independent ice cream manufacturer, the trade tensions have coincided with some of its best summer sales.The family-run company employs 1,150 people in Markdale, Ontario, about two hours north-west of Toronto. Ashley Chapman, the company’s chief operating officer, said the business had benefited as Canadians turned towards local products.“Every time Trump insults Canada, Canadians buy more Canadian things,” Ashley Chapman, chief operating officer for Chapman’s ice cream told the Financial Times.“It actually has worked out quite well for us.”The company has also been changing where it gets its ingredients and components. Since March last year, when Trump launched his first round of tariffs on Canada, it has been looking for suppliers outside the US.More than 70% of its American ingredients and components are expected to be replaced with Canadian or non-US sources by mid-2027.“If you had asked me two years ago, ‘what about sourcing your almonds from Australia?’ [instead of the US] I would have said you were insane,” he said.“It’s no great surprise that Trump is pushing for more concessions, more everything. But certainly Canadians have had enough,” he said. “The buy Canadian movement is strong and getting stronger.”Ottawa-based Maker House, a retail and online gift store, has spent the past 18 months selling 300 Canadian-made products. The business also stopped sending products to the US after tariffs increased its costs.“We had a really good year last year and then I think this past week we’ve had a good lift for sure,” said owner Gareth Davies.Among its most popular products were items carrying the slogan “elbows up”, Prime Minister Mark Carney’s battle cry for resisting Trump’s hostility towards Canada.“Everything in the store is made in Canada, you don’t need to worry and check the labels,” Davies said.“All this is a reminder that we can do better to protect our own economy by supporting Canadians who are making things,” he said.The shift has also been felt in Ontario’s wine industry.When American alcohol was taken off the shelves of Ontario’s government-run alcohol stores in response to Trump’s March 2025 tariffs, local producers saw a “significant boost” in demand as consumers embraced the ‘buy local’ sentiment.At Leaning Post Wines in Niagara, near Lake Ontario, sales increased by 3,000 cases.“We saw an additional 3,000 cases of wine sold. When you only make 8,000 cases, that’s a significant increase,” said Nadia Senchuk who runs Leaning Post Wines with her husband Ilya in Niagara, near Lake Ontario.“Our growth was great over the past 18 months,” she said.Ontario has nearly 200 wineries, which contribute more than C$5.5bn to the Canadian economy each year and employ 22,000 people, according to the Vintners Quality Alliance, a trade group. Sales of VQA wine were up 10% year on year last year.The change in trade ties is also creating opportunities for Canadian manufacturers supplying defence-related products.Ontario-based Wuxly began by making coats for Canada’s freezing winters. It now produces defence- and aerospace-grade clothing for a number of military forces around the world.Its workforce of operating seamsters and seamstresses grew from 50 in 2024 to 200 in 2025. The company expects that number to cross 350 by the end of this year.Wuxly is hoping to benefit from greater local procurement in Canadian defence spending, replacing some demand for US suppliers.“We’ve definitely seen more interest in Canadian-made defence textiles under the Build–Partner–Buy framework set out in the defence industrial strategy,” said James Yurichuk, Wuxly’s founder and CEO.The company has also been looking towards Europe as Canada pivots away from US markets. It sent more than 250,000 Canadian-made goods to the EU last year and was “tracking to surpass this number” in 2026.“Perhaps the biggest silver lining of the trade war, and of the broader cooling in relations with the US, has been the heightened interest from European Nato nations,” Yurichuk said.“There’s still real work to do in supporting domestic champions but we’re heading in the right direction,” he added.However, every business is finding the shift easy. Joey Walsh, owner of HockeyStickMan, a hockey equipment retailer, told FT that almost half of the company’s sales had previously come from the US.The family business operates stores in Toronto and Belleville in eastern Ontario and employs around 80 people. It sells equipment from brands including CCM and Bauer, along with its own Pro Blackout line, which is mostly made in China and avoids many of Trump’s latest duties.“Tariffs have affected our business significantly, but we’re doing everything we can to hold the line and not pass costs on to our customers,” he said.“Tariffs are charged based on where a product is made, not who sells it, so thankfully this round of tariffs has less impact on the industry than it appears to at surface level,” he added.Even where the direct impact of tariffs is limited, Walsh said businesses are facing extra work and costs because tariff levels keep changing. Customs, logistics and paperwork have all added to the strain.“It has gotten more expensive to operate, for us and for the industry as a whole. That pressure isn’t finished,” he said.
Article Summary: Canadian PM Mark Carney has warned that moving away from the US as Canada’s biggest trading partner ‘will come at a cost’ The new Canadian levies cover nearly C$28 billion ($20 billion) of American products, ranging from steel and furniture to cotton T-shirts.

Article Title: Consumer durables drive customer growth
Article Text:
Representative image

MUMBAI: India's retail credit market is showing a widening gap between the number of borrowers being added and the value of loans being accumulated, with consumer durable loans driving new borrower acquisition, while home and gold loans account for much of the portfolio growth.According to credit bureau CRIF's 'How India Lends' report, gold loan outstandings jumped 62.2% to Rs 21.7 lakh crore, while home loan outstandings rose 10.5% year-on-year to Rs 45.5 lakh crore in Q1 FY27. Yet origination volumes (new disbursements) for gold loans fell 4.5% year-on-year to 3.7 crore, while home loans grew by a modest 6.4% to 8.3 lakh. Quarter-on-quarter, gold and home loan volumes dropped 25.6% and 17.3%, respectively.Consumer durable loans, however, grew both in volume and value. The origination volume grew 27.4% year-on-year to 2.9 crore, while the origination value grew 36.6%, with portfolio outstanding reaching Rs 1.2 lakh crore as of June 2026 from Rs 89,300 crore a year earlier. Consumer loans also defied the seasonal trend, growing 21.4% from Rs 1,00,500 crore as of March 2026. Consumer durables accounted for 45.5% of all new-to-credit borrower volumes in India, more than twice the share of gold loans at 18.3% and personal loans at 18.2%.
Article Summary: India's retail credit market is showing a widening gap between the number of borrowers being added and the value of loans being accumulated. Consumer durable loans, however, grew both in volume and value. Consumer durables accounted for 45.5% of all new-to-credit borrower volumes in India, more than twice the share of gold loans.

Article Title: AI corners 80% of all global equity funding in March quarter
Article Text:
Representational image

MUMBAI: Whether AI will get us all killed by the end of the decade is still a matter of debate, but funding into artificial intelligence continues to soar.In fact, it is only getting bigger. Global AI funding touched a whopping $226 billion in the March quarter this year. That's almost 80% of all global equity funding, showed a study by Boston Consulting Group (BCG). This pie stood at 41% in the year-ago period and at just about 15% in CY2022, explaining the pace at which investor dollars are chasing AI. American AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic have contributed to the bulk of this investment surge with their massive fundraises earlier this year. In March, OpenAI raised $122 billion at a post-money valuation of $852 billion while Anthropic bagged $30 billion in capital from investors in Feb at a valuation of $380 billion.Call it ironical or not but both Anthropic and OpenAI which are at the forefront of AI innovation have come under scrutiny for unethical practices. Earlier this week, Jacob Coxon, a researcher with Anthropic, quit the firm, raising concerns over the risks that come with the unfettered rise of AI. "They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives....the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade," Coxon said on X.About 65% of AI equity funding has been cornered by foundation models and platforms in 2026 (Jan-Jun period), up from a mere 4% in 2022. "Investors are concentrating bets on the intelligence layer of the AI stack," analysts at BCG said.
Article Summary: Global AI funding touched a whopping $226 billion in the March quarter this year. That's almost 80% of all global equity funding, showed a study by Boston Consulting Group. American AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic have contributed to the bulk of this investment surge.

Article Title: FM calls for tech body for stronger global voice
Article Text:
FM Sitharaman at Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai

MUMBAI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman called upon tech companies to promote a federated industry platform to give India's technology sector a stronger collective voice in global markets and regulatory discussions."There may be merit in considering a federated industry platform that brings together the broader Indian technology ecosystem," Sitharaman said at Global Fintech Fest. Such a platform, she said, should not speak over individual companies but provide the sector with "a credible collective voice internationally".Sitharaman also hit back at critics who question the sustainability of India's growth, dismissing them as "naraz phuphas" who are never short of reasons to doubt the country's momentum and the capabilities of its young population. She said such critics were debating on television whether India's demographic dividend had slipped away or turned into a burden, relying on "vibecasting", rather than actual numbers. In contrast, she said, young Indians were bypassing the cynicism, building enterprises and demonstrating that the country's demographic advantage was already an "active, unstoppable reality".Meanwhile, the platform could engage foreign govts and regulators early, before regulatory positions harden and barriers are erected, she said.It could also identify areas where standards can remain interoperable, share best practices on data and cybersecurity, and help Indian companies navigate different licensing regimes.Sitharaman's statement comes days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for linking India's domestic payment networks with those of other countries. RBI and govt are also keen on enabling cross-border transactions using central bank digital currencies.Sitharaman said the platform could represent Indian industry in discussions where international rules governing emerging technologies are being shaped. It could also help Indian companies commercialise and monetise their intellectual property across jurisdictions, build partnerships overseas and enter new markets with greater confidence.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman called upon tech companies to promote a federated industry platform to give India's technology sector a stronger collective voice. Such a platform, she said, should not speak over individual companies but provide the sector with "a credible collective voice internationally" She also hit back at critics who question the sustainability of India's growth.

Article Title: Days after Bhatt, another director quits Coforge board
Article Text:
OP Bhatt

Boardroom shake-up

BENGALURU: Boardroom turmoil at Coforge has deepened with independent director and Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) chair DK Singh resigning days after chairman OP Bhatt stepped down amid an internal audit that flagged concerns over how board-evaluation findings were presented to directors.Singh resigned with immediate effect, citing "differences and tension" between independent and executive directors and concerns over possible changes in strategy, transparency and compensation. His exit comes as the internal audit and governance review, which led the board to seek explanations from both Bhatt and Singh, remains open.Bhatt's resignation followed a KPMG internal audit that flagged procedural lapses in how Coforge's board-evaluation reports were shared with directors, including the withholding of the lowest rating given to the chairman, according to people familiar with the matter.The audit found that detailed board-evaluation reports were available only to Bhatt and the NRC chair and were not shared with other directors, including independent directors. The reports were presented to the NRC and board without copies being circulated, the sources said.More significantly, the chairman's category received the lowest rating in the evaluation, but this was not disclosed or discussed with the NRC or board, they said.Calls and text messages to Bhatt did not elicit a response by press time.The issue surfaced when KPMG reviewed governance processes as part of its Q2 FY26 internal-audit plan. According to the sources, Bhatt instructed the company secretary not to circulate the detailed reports to other directors. The NRC chair subsequently presented the findings jointly with Bhatt at NRC and board meetings, giving the board the impression that the evaluation had produced broadly positive results despite several sections receiving low scores, the sources said.The development led the board to seek an explanation from Bhatt, who resigned on September 8 before the review was concluded.In his resignation email dated Sept 10, Singh said the recent events had made it difficult for him to continue discharging his responsibilities at the organisation."When I joined the Board in 2024, it was transitioning from a private equity-led Board to a more independent Board. While I believe that transition was moving in the right direction, it also created some differences and tension, particularly between the Independent and Executive Directors," Singh said.
Article Summary: Independent director and Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) chair DK Singh resigns days after chairman OP Bhatt stepped down. Bhatt's resignation followed a KPMG internal audit that flagged procedural lapses in how Coforge's board-evaluation reports were shared with directors.

Article Title: Algorithms must explain decisions, says Murmu
Article Text:
RBI deputy governor SC Murmu

MUMBAI: Reserve Bank of India wants lenders to ensure that algorithms used to make or materially influence credit decisions can explain why a borrower has been rejected, putting accountability and explainability at the centre of its expectations for lending that's driven by technology.RBI deputy governor Shirish Chandra Murmu, speaking at the Global FinTech Fest in Mumbai on Friday, said digital lending should not merely make the process of extending credit faster. Technology and better data should help lenders reach borrowers who have historically remained outside the formal financial system, making credit "better" as well as faster."The vendor with the printed QR code is now part of the formal financial system. The questions she faces next are harder ones. Will she be offered credit on terms she can understand? If an algorithm declines her loan application, will anyone be able to tell her why? If her account is frozen by a fraud detection system, how long before she can trade again? Those questions are the real content of trusted innovation, and how we answer them will matter more than any technology we deploy," said Murmu.He cautioned institutions against being comfortable with their cryptographic dependencies. He said that while quantum computing is not an immediate threat, payment infrastructure has long tech cycles and migration to new standards takes years. "There is also the 'harvest now, decrypt later' risk, under which encrypted information collected today becomes accessible as computing capability advances."
Article Summary: RBI deputy governor Shirish Chandra Murmu said digital lending should not merely make the process of extending credit faster. Technology and better data should help lenders reach borrowers who have historically remained outside the formal financial system. Murmu cautioned institutions against being comfortable with their cryptographic dependencies.

Article Title: NSE reduces public offer size to 22.6k crore, issue opens Sept 17
Article Text:
NSE

Pocketing multi-bagger returns

MUMBAI: The much-awaited NSE IPO will open on Sept 17 and close on Sept 21 with the listing slotted for Sept 24, the bourse said on Friday. With some of the existing shareholders together selling a 5.1% stake in the country's largest stock exchange, at the upper end of the Rs 1,700-1,785/share price band, the IPO would be worth Rs 22,568 crore.At the upper end of the price band, NSE will command a valuation of Rs 4.4 lakh crore, putting it in the league of companies like Hindustan Unilever (current market capitalisation of Rs 4.5 lakh crore), Titan (Rs 4.4 lakh crore) and Sun Pharma (Rs 4.4 lakh crore).In the IPO, a total of 23 NSE shareholders together are selling a little over 12.6 crore shares of the bourse. The selling shareholders include State Bank of India, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, Aranda Investments (Mauritius), MS Strategic (Mauritius), The New India Assurance, SBI Capital Markets, Bank of Baroda, Stock Holding Corp of India, General Insurance Corp, and United India Insurance.At Rs 22,568 crore, NSE's IPO would be the second biggest such offer in India, behind Hyundai India's Rs 27,800-crore IPO that closed towards the end of 2024. Earlier, NSE's IPO was expected to raise about Rs 30,000 crore, which would have made it the largest IPO in India.On Sept 4, markets regulator Sebi had cleared NSE's IPO documents. During the launch of the bourse's IPO, Ashishkumar Chauhan, CEO & MD, NSE, said that earlier, in the run-up to the offer, some of its existing investors were willing to sell a higher quantum of shares in the IPO.But closer to the launch of the offer, some shareholders expressed their willingness to part with a lesser number of NSE shares.Those shareholders may have done so in expectation of some upside in the future, Chauhan said. When asked about the price band for the IPO, Chauhan said that it was decided by the merchant bankers who are advising the bourse. "After deliberations and roadshows across the world, our merchant bankers have advised us that this is the price," he said.The shares of NSE will be listed only on BSE since Sebi doesn't allow self-listing, meaning an exchange cannot list its own shares on its trading platform. Likewise, BSE is traded only on NSE.However, there's a provision of 'permitted to trade' segment on the bourses. Under this category, even if a stock is not listed, the bourse could allow it to trade on its platform. When asked, Chauhan said that NSE has not written to the regulator to explore such an option for NSE shares to get traded on its own platform.Some of the early investors in NSE, all PSUs, are making up to 5,578 times return in the offer.On Friday, in the unofficial market for stocks, the grey market premium (GMP), the mark-up the NSE stocks could command on listing over the offer price, was Rs 218 per share, indicating a listing price of Rs 2,003. Depending on market conditions and investors' response to an IPO, GMP keeps fluctuating till the time of listing.
Article Summary: The much-awaited NSE IPO will open on Sept 17 and close on Sept 21 with the listing slotted for Sept 24. At the upper end of the Rs 1,700-1,785/share price band, the IPO would be worth Rs 22,568 crore. The shares of NSE will be listed only on BSE since Sebi doesn't allow self-listing.

Article Title: Nine IPOs attract bids worth 1.4 lakh crore
Article Text:
IPO

Buzzing with activity

MUMBAI: In one of the busiest weeks for the primary market in recent times, six mainboard IPOs closed on Friday, along with three on SME platforms of the two bourses. The nine primary offers together saw total demand worth about Rs 1.4 lakh crore against a mobilisation target of about Rs 3,100 crore, bidding data on NSE and BSE showed.The biggest offer to close on Friday was by RentoMojo, which is raising a total of Rs 1,250 crore, with the post-anchor part pegged at Rs 871 crore. The bidding (post-anchor) part of the issue was subscribed 73 times, generating a total demand worth nearly Rs 63,600 crore. Among the nine IPOs that closed Friday, this was the biggest generator in terms of value.The day also saw Karamtara Engineering's issue subscribed 60 times, with the post-anchor demand valued at Rs 40,667 crore, bidding data showed. Among other IPOs that closed during the day, demand for LCC Projects was worth Rs 14,817 crore, for ARCIL Rs 10,311 crore and for Steamhouse India Rs 9,299 crore.
Article Summary: Six mainboard IPOs closed on Friday, along with three on SME platforms. The nine primary offers together saw total demand worth about Rs 1.4 lakh crore. The biggest offer to close on Friday was by RentoMojo, raising a total of Rs 1,250 crore.

Article Title: RBI moves to suck out excess liquidity
Article Text:
RBI

Highest weekly increases

Exploring oprions: RBI

Eye on inflation

MUMBAI: The $136.4 billion raised by banks from non-residents and foreign lenders, then swapped with RBI, has swelled India's foreign-exchange reserves by a record $44.9 billion to $785.7 billion in the week ended Sept 4. The windfall gives RBI a larger war chest to defend the rupee, but creates a problem at home with too much cash in the banking system.RBI is now trying to mop up that liquidity. On Friday, it announced a Rs 1 lakh crore open-market sale of govt bonds, turning a successful foreign-currency fund-raising exercise into a domestic liquidity-management headache.RBI will sell Rs 1 lakh crore of govt bonds maturing in FY29-32 in three tranches on Sept 17, 21 and 28 to drain surplus liquidity. This is its first net bond sale in two years. Bond yields rose after the announcement, with the 10-year yield up six basis points to 7.04% and the five-year yield nearly 10 basis points to 6.62%.Banks raised $127 billion through the special forex mobilisation scheme, creating surplus rupee liquidity and pushing overnight rates below the repo rate. Markets had expected measures including FX swaps, MSS bonds, OMO sales and a possible CRR hike.In an interview with a TV channel, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said the central bank had several options to manage liquidity beyond VRRR, including open market operations and FX swaps. He said "nothing is off the table." RBI has also been using dollar-rupee swaps to reduce banks' rupee holdings. FCNR(B) deposits mobilised through the recently concluded RBI swap facility totalled $127.2 billion. Malhotra said the flows were "very robust" and reflected strong investor confidence in India's macroeconomic fundamentals. He said the exercise showed that foreign capital could be mobilised within a short period and strengthened financial stability and external sector resilience.He also said the inflows had helped stabilise the forex market. "It has given us the liquidity at the same time, and it has improved sentiments," he said. Nearly half of the deposits, or around 48.5-50%, have a five-year tenure. About 42% fall in the three-to-four-year maturity bracket and around 9% in the four-to-five-year window. Some of the liquidity will be withdrawn automatically over time, he said. Higher crude prices remain a risk to inflation.Malhotra said the impact would depend on the extent to which higher costs are passed through. "Crude has gone up. July was for the Indian basket an average of $82 (per barrel). Aug it has gone up to $90 (per barrel) and so that will certainly have some impact, but it will depend again on the pass-through," he said.Malhotra said govt had absorbed and cushioned much of the oil shock, helping the economy weather the impact. RBI will continue to watch inflation persistence, expectations and generalisation ahead of the next monetary policy committee meeting on Oct 5-7. "I mean, risks are there on both sides... The MPC will make a reassessment of the growth-inflation dynamics when it meets in a month or so. Let me not give my assessment," he said.
Article Summary: India's foreign-exchange reserves swelled by a record $44.9 billion to $785.7 billion in the week ended Sept 4. The windfall gives RBI a larger war chest to defend the rupee, but creates a problem at home with too much cash in the banking system.

Article Title: Higher value drives gold and home loan growth, borrower addition slows
Article Text:
Consumer durable loans are driving new borrower acquisition, while home and gold loans are driving portfolio growth

MUMBAI: India’s retail credit market is showing a widening gap between the number of borrowers being added and the value of loans being accumulated, with consumer durable loans driving new borrower acquisition while home and gold loans account for much of the portfolio growth.According to credit bureau CRIF's `How India Lends' report, home loan outstandings rose 10.5% year-on-year to Rs 45.5 lakh crore in Q1 FY27, while gold loan outstandings jumped 62.2% to Rs 21.7 lakh crore. Yet origination volumes for the two categories fell 17.3% and 25.6% quarter-on-quarter respectively, to 8.3 lakh home loans and 369.9 lakh gold loans.Consumer durable loans followed the opposite pattern. Originations rose 25.6% quarter-on-quarter to 287.0 lakh loans and 27.4% year-on-year. The segment accounted for 45.5% of all New-to-Credit borrower volumes in India, more than twice the share of gold loans at 18.3% and personal loans at 18.2%.The difference is reflected in ticket sizes. Consumer durable loans had an average ticket size of Rs 22,303 and accounted for just 0.7% of total consumption credit, with an outstanding portfolio of Rs 1.22 lakh crore. The Rs 10,000 to Rs 25,000 bracket accounted for 41.0% of originations, while loans between Rs 25,000 and Rs 50,000 accounted for another 23.4%.The segment’s active accounts rose 8.9% year-on-year to 11.3 crore. Lending also continued to spread beyond the largest cities, with Beyond Top 100 cities accounting for 43.5% of origination value in Q1 FY27, up from 40.8% a year earlier.Home loans, by contrast, are increasingly concentrated in larger-ticket borrowing. Loans above Rs 75 lakh accounted for 41.0% of origination value in Q1 FY27, up from 36.8% in Q4 FY25. Active home loan accounts increased only 3.9% year-on-year to 238.4 lakh, while originations fell from 10.1 lakh in the previous quarter to 8.3 lakh. First-time credit seekers accounted for just 1.0% of total New-to-Credit originations.Gold loans showed an even sharper divergence between volume and value. Loans above Rs 5 lakh accounted for 38.2% of origination value while representing only 9.1% of originations by volume. The average ticket size rose 37.5% year-on-year to Rs 2.17 lakh, helped by higher bullion prices and tiered Loan-to-Value limits.Although gold loan originations fell 25.6% quarter-on-quarter from 497.3 lakh to 369.9 lakh, their value increased 47.3% year-on-year to Rs 6,47,417 crore. The active portfolio rose 16.4% quarter-on-quarter and 62.2% year-on-year to Rs 21.70 lakh crore.The contrasting patterns suggest a two-stage lending funnel. NBFCs use point-of-sale consumer durable loans to source 87.4% of volume, providing low-ticket digital entry points for new borrowers. As borrowers establish repayment histories with credit bureaus, banks and housing financiers can offer larger home and collateralised gold loans, using rising asset values and larger ticket sizes to expand portfolios without a proportionate increase in new borrowers.
Article Summary: India's retail credit market is showing a widening gap between the number of borrowers being added and the value of loans being accumulated. Consumer durable loans are driving new borrower acquisition while home and gold loans account for much of the portfolio growth. Home loan outstandings rose 10.5% year-on-year to Rs 45.5 lakh crore in Q1 FY27.

Article Title: India-EU FTA draft: European cars, wine, farm goods set for lower tariffs; key points
Article Text:
India’s FTA with the EU will offer European automakers concessional tariffs on passenger vehicles, with annual quotas rising to 1.6 lakh, alongside tariff concessions on wines and select agricultural products.

What changes for EU cars

EVs, wine and farm products

GTRI flags wider implications

European carmakers will get a significantly wider opening to India’s passenger vehicle market under the proposed India-EU free trade agreement, with the draft pact released on Friday providing for concessional import duties on up to 1 lakh cars in the first year. The quota will gradually rise to 1.6 lakh vehicles from the 10th year of implementation.The draft text provides tariff-rate quotas (TRQs) for EU-origin internal-combustion engine (ICE) and hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), with the concessional duty linked to the vehicle’s CIF value. The agreement is expected to be signed by the end of this year and could come into force next year, reported PTI.The concessions will apply only to passenger vehicles priced at Euro 15,000 (around Rs 16.6 lakh) or more. Cars below that threshold will continue to face the existing tariff.For vehicles priced between Euro 15,000 and Euro 35,000 (around Rs 16.6 lakh to Rs 38.8 lakh), the in-quota duty will fall from 110 per cent to 35 per cent in the first year and then to 10 per cent by the fifth year.For cars priced above Euro 35,000, the duty will fall from the existing most-favoured-nation tariff of 66 per cent to 30 per cent in the first year and eventually to 10 per cent.The overall quota for ICE and hybrid passenger cars will rise from 1 lakh units in the first year to 1.07 lakh in the second year, 1.15 lakh in the third, 1.225 lakh in the fourth and 1.3 lakh in the fifth year. It will then increase progressively to 1.6 lakh vehicles from the 10th year.From the fifth year, 43,000 vehicles will be reserved for cars priced above Euro 50,000 (around Rs 55.4 lakh).India will also gradually lower tariffs on EU cars imported outside the quota. For cars priced between Euro 15,000 and Euro 50,000, the out-of-quota duty will eventually fall to 35 per cent by the 10th year, while the duty on cars priced above Euro 50,000 will fall to 30 per cent.The pact also provides a separate quota for completely knocked-down ICE and hybrid vehicles. The quota will stand at 75,000 units annually for the first five years before gradually declining to 50,000 units from the 10th year. The in-quota duty will fall from 13.75 per cent in the first year to 8.25 per cent from the third year, against the current 16.5 per cent.Concessions for battery-electric vehicles, plug-in hybrids and other eligible technologies will begin from the fifth year. They will apply only to vehicles priced at Euro 20,000 (around Rs 22 lakh) or more.The CBU quota for these vehicles will start at 20,000 units in the fifth year, rise to 50,000 in the 10th year and reach 90,000 from the 14th year onwards. The in-quota duty will fall from 30 per cent in the fifth year to 10 per cent in the 10th year, compared with the listed base duty of 110 per cent. Vehicles below the Euro 20,000 price threshold will not receive the concession.The draft pact also offers tariff concessions on selected EU agricultural and food products, including wine, pork, apples, kiwifruit, pears and peaches, largely through quotas and price-based conditions.For wine, products valued below Euro 2.50 per 750 ml will receive no concession and will continue to face the 150 per cent base customs duty. Wine priced between Euro 2.50 and Euro 10 will see the duty fall to 75 per cent in the first year and to 30 per cent from the eighth year. For wine priced at Euro 10 or more, the duty will progressively fall to 20 per cent from the eighth year.India will also allow 2,000 metric tonnes of EU pork annually at concessional rates, while the quota for apples will start at 50,000 tonnes and rise to 1 lakh tonnes from the 11th year, subject to a minimum CIF price of Rs 80 per kg.The first-year quota for kiwifruit will be 12,000 tonnes, rising to 15,000 tonnes from the 11th year. Pears will have a fixed annual quota of 2,250 tonnes, while the quota for peaches will be limited to 20 tonnes a year.The concessions mark a significant opening of some of India’s sensitive markets under the proposed FTA.GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava said the EU had become the second major trade partner after the UK to secure automotive tariff concessions from India under an FTA.“Having established these precedents, India should soon receive similar demands for preferential market access and generous TRQs from other key trade partners such as Japan and South Korea,” he said.Srivastava noted that India imported only 17,191 cars from the EU in 2025, while the agreement provides European automakers with a first-year quota of 1 lakh completely built-up ICE and non-plug-in hybrid cars.“That is almost six times current imports,” he said.He said India had opened parts of several sensitive markets through tariff-rate quotas and price-based concessions rather than unrestricted tariff cuts.“These commitments cover automobiles, wine and selected alcoholic products, pork, apples, kiwifruit, pears and peaches. Imports meeting the prescribed origin, price and quantity conditions will enter at lower duties, while most imports outside these limits will continue to face the normal tariff,” he said.
Article Summary: The draft text provides tariff-rate quotas for EU-origin internal-combustion engine (ICE) and hybrid electric vehicles. The agreement is expected to be signed by the end of this year and could come into force next year. The concessions will apply only to passenger vehicles priced at Euro 15,000 (around Rs 16.6 lakh) or more.

Article Title: 6 new coal mines to start operations this fiscal year
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Six new captive and commercial mines are expected to commence operations in this fiscal year, while three have already started production, govt said on Friday, as 59 thermal power plants face a shortage of fuel due to high electricity demand and disruptions in supplies during the monsoon.Coal ministry, in a statement, said captive mines have been a mainstay of fuel production, with their output growing by over 10% in a year from 167 million tonnes in 2024-25 to 184 MT in 2025-26. Till Sept 10 this year, coal production from captive mines has grown by about 5% year-on-year to 69 MT, against 66 MT in the corresponding period last year. The period also includes the monsoon season, when mining and evacuation of coal become difficult.“Along with commercial mines, which produced nearly 26 MT, the captive and commercial segment together accounted for 210 MT in FY 2025-26 against 191 MT the previous year,” the statement read.Captive and commercial mines account for about 21% of total domestic coal production, which stood at 1,039 MT in FY26 and remained above one billion tonnes for the second year running, the ministry said.State-run Coal India Limited (CIL) has offered power plants having fuel supply agreements with it and its subsidiaries the option to lift additional quantities of coal, over and above the quantities stipulated in their annual contracts, as stocks at thermal power plants fell further.Govt has also increased the number of rakes to 444 to ramp up coal supplies to power plants from the mines of CIL and its subsidiaries, as well as captive mine operators.
Article Summary: Captive and commercial mines account for about 21% of total domestic coal production. 59 thermal power plants face a shortage of fuel due to high electricity demand and disruptions in supplies during the monsoon. State-run Coal India Limited has offered power plants having fuel supply agreements with it and its subsidiaries the option to lift additional quantities of coal.

Article Title: Coforge boardroom rift deepens as NRC chair Singh quits
Article Text:
Boardroom with human resource business people writing paper negotiating a contract.

Bengaluru: Coforge boardroom tensions deepen as independent director and Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) chair DK Singh resigned with immediate effect, citing “differences and tension” between independent and executive directors and concerns over changes in strategy, transparency and compensation. Singh’s resignation comes days after chairman OP Bhatt stepped down and amid an internal audit review that the company says raised concerns involving the board chairman and NRC chair.In his resignation email on Thursday, Singh said the recent events made it difficult for him to continue discharging his responsibilities as an independent director. “When I joined the Board in 2024, it was transitioning from a private equity-led Board to a more independent Board. While I believe that transition was moving in the right direction, it also created some differences and tension, particularly between the Independent and Executive Directors,” Singh said.He said the addition of new board members could bring “changes in direction and priorities in areas such as strategy, transparency, and compensation et al.” “While I welcome constructive debate and different viewpoints, I believe the current circumstances may make it increasingly difficult for me to effectively fulfill my responsibilities as an independent director and, most importantly, to exercise the independent judgement I believe is necessary to act in the best interests of the company and all of its shareholders,” Singh said.Coforge, however, strongly disputed his account, saying the allegation of differences and tension between independent and executive directors was “unfounded” and appeared to be an “afterthought”. The company said that since 2024, all business strategy and governance decisions had been approved unanimously, with board minutes reflecting “cohesion and unanimity”.The board also said Singh’s resignation followed concerns identified in the internal audit review and the subsequent process of seeking explanations from the chairman and NRC chair. “It is apparent that the NRC Chair has resigned as a consequence of these events,” it said.Vivek Sharma will serve as interim chair until January 31, 2027, lead a global search for additional independent directors and oversee the election of a new chair. Beth Boucher has been appointed NRC chair.
Article Summary: Coforge boardroom tensions deepen as independent director and Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) chair DK Singh resigns. Singh’s resignation comes days after chairman OP Bhatt stepped down and amid an internal audit review that the company says raised concerns.

Article Title: Houthi advances puts India and global trade closer to the edge
Article Text:
Houthi militants seized Yemen's Mocha port, threatening vital global energy supplies

The TOI correspondent from Washington:

Rapid advances by Iran-backed Houthis along Yemen's Red Sea coast is bringing the group dangerously close to controlling another key maritime chokepoint in the region, raising fresh concerns from New Delhi to Washington to European capitals in between about the security of global trade, energy supplies, and shipping.Reports from the region on Friday that Houthi forces had reached Perim – or Mayun – Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait after Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces withdrew from the strategically located outpost sent alarms in the global strategic affairs community even as the Trump establishment was in the throes of a Republican political fiesta in Dallas.The developments follow the reported Houthi capture of Mocha, a strategically important Red Sea port whose coffee beans infused regions as far apart as Chikmagalur and Seattle. The gains bring the Houthis – named after its late founder Hussein Badreddin al-Houthi but otherwise known as Ansar Allah (supporters of god) -- substantially closer to Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow waterway connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.For New Delhi, this development brings even greater headache following the Strait of Hormuz fiasco. Bab el-Mandeb is effectively the western gateway to India's maritime neighborhood and an essential link in the sea route connecting India with Europe through the Suez Canal.Any sustained Houthi ability to threaten or disrupt shipping through the strait could increase freight rates, insurance costs and transit times for Indian exporters and importers. Ships avoiding the Red Sea would instead need to make the much longer journey around the Cape of Good Hope.India's exposure is particularly significant because its refineries have become major suppliers of petroleum products to Europe. A prolonged disruption would therefore affect India not merely through the cost of imports but also through the economics of one of its important export markets. If both Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb become constrained, the world's energy and shipping system would face a potentially unprecedented pincer around two critical maritime arteries.The developments come as the US artificial-intelligence company Anthropic reported that a Houthi-linked group in northern Yemen used its Claude AI model in work on missile and rocket systems -- a reminder that the movement's military capabilities are evolving even as its forces make significant gains on the ground.The battlefield successes of Houthis -- dismissed initially as flip-flop wearing desperadoes -- have generated a torrent of dramatic claims on social media, including assertions that Saudi forces surrendered to Houthis and the Iran-backed group has captured large quantities of American military equipment. Videos and photographs appeared to show Houthi fighters with US-manufactured Oshkosh M-ATV armored vehicles that had been supplied to Saudi-backed Yemeni forces. Much of the most dramatic material originates from Houthi sources or their supporters, ridiculed as photoshop experts by western analysts.Still, reports of Houthi success have alarmed some experts in Washington. “The Houthis’ rapid advance is just the beginning of the blowback effects we are now going to face as a result of our counterproductive policies in the Middle East & because of this senseless war in Iran,” noted Joe Kent, Former Director of the National Counterterrorism Center who has been advocating an end to U.S foreign military entanglements.Indeed there have been reports that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman sought US strikes against the Houthis and that President Trump declined the request, rebuffing two "desperate" phone calls. Washington’s reluctance to get embroiled even more in the region reflects the central problem confronting U.S: how to protect freedom of navigation and support Saudi security without becoming drawn into another open-ended military campaign in Yemen.The Houthis have demonstrated in recent years that they do not need conventional military superiority to impose disproportionate costs. Drones and relatively inexpensive missiles can force heavily armed commercial vessels to alter their routes, while the threat itself can raise insurance and shipping costs. Control of territory around Bab el-Mandeb Strait and its approaches gives them a much stronger position from which to monitor, threaten and potentially disrupt shipping. That could have profound consequences for India, which has already deployed naval assets to protect merchant shipping during previous Houthi attacks.The Anthropic disclosure adds a potentially important technological dimension after the company said the Yemen-based group used Claude to assist with weapons projects, including guidance, navigation and control software. Anthropic did not establish that AI had enabled the Houthis to field a new operational missile, but the episode illustrates how AI could lower the technical barriers facing non-state weapons developers.The Houthi success also creates immediate geopolitical complications for Pakistan, which is both a major defense partner of Saudi Arabia and has sought to maintain channels with Iran. A new defense arrangement involving Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey that an armed attack on one member is to be regarded as an attack on all three creates a potentially awkward test for Rawalpindi. While a Pakistani military intervention against the Houthis would put Islamabad into direct conflict with an Iran-backed movement, potentially damaging its relationship with Tehran, standing aside could raise questions about the practical meaning of its new security commitment to Riyadh.
Article Summary: Houthi militants seized Yemen's Mocha port, threatening vital global energy supplies. The gains bring the Houthis substantially closer to Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow waterway connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean. A prolonged disruption would affect India not merely through the cost of imports but also through the economics of one of its important export markets.

Article Title: BRICS Summit 2026: Traffic curbs, diversions in Delhi from 2pm to 8.30pm today; check key routes
Article Text:
Traffic restrictions will be in place across central Delhi roads for the BRICS Summit.





NEW DELHI: Traffic restrictions and diversions will come into force across several key roads in central Delhi as the BRICS Summit 2026 gets underway at Bharat Mandapam, Pragati Maidan.The Delhi Traffic Police has issued an advisory for 2pm to 8.30pm on September 11, with traffic to be regulated at 22 diversion points and restrictions likely on more than 35 roads. The focus will be on diverting traffic away from routes being used for the movement of summit delegates.Major roads under regulation include Mathura Road, Sardar Patel Marg, Mother Teresa Crescent, Teen Murti Marg, Akbar Road, Tees January Marg, Rajesh Pilot Marg, Subramaniam Bharti Marg, Moti Lal Nehru Marg, Dr Zakir Hussain Marg, Africa Avenue Road, Satya Marg, Shanti Path, Janpath, Ashoka Road, Barakhamba Road, Tolstoy Marg, Ranjeet Singh Flyover, Niti Marg, Panchsheel Marg, K.G. Marg, PWD Abdul Kalam Road, Press Enclave Road, Lal Bahadur Shastri Marg, Josef Broz Tito Marg and Lala Lajpat Rai Marg.At Dinesh Nandini Dalmia Chowk, traffic towards Mathura Road and Tilak Marg will not be allowed beyond the junction. At Ram Charan Aggarwal Chowk, commercial vehicles will not be allowed beyond the junction towards W-Point. Diversions will also be in place at Mir Dard Chowk, Kasturba Gandhi Marg, Janpath, Patel Chowk, RML Hospital roundabout and Vande Mataram Marg.Traffic police have also placed advance signage at key junctions, including ITO, warning commuters not to proceed beyond restricted points.With government offices and schools shut for the day, traffic officials expect the restrictions to have limited impact on regular daytime movement.Commuters have been advised to plan their journeys in advance, avoid restricted corridors and use public transport wherever possible.
Article Summary: Delhi Traffic Police issues advisory for 2pm to 8.30pm on September 11. Traffic to be regulated at 22 diversion points and restrictions likely on more than 35 roads. Focus will be on diverting traffic away from routes being used for movement of summit delegates.

Article Title: 'Smashed heads with stone': Jaipur man kills wife, 3 daughters; flees after collecting milk from delivery man
Article Text:
A man allegedly killed his wife and three daughters in Jaipur's Kardhani area.





JAIPUR: A man allegedly killed his wife and three daughters by repeatedly striking them on the head with a stone at their home in Jaipur’s Kardhani area early Friday, then fled after collecting milk from a deliveryman, police said.The victims were identified as Geeta Jha and her daughters Nandini, Radhika and Gauri. Their bodies were found at thier house in Govind Vatika after police received information around 10am.Police said preliminary investigation pointed to a possible family dispute as the motive. Police and an FSL team reached the house and began examining the scene.Investigators suspect Rahul attacked the four while they were asleep, using a stone. Police said blood at the scene appeared to have been wiped with clothes after the killings.According to police, Rahul collected milk from the milkman around 7am and fled soon afterwards. His elderly father was found inside the house.Police are searching for Rahul and are examining the circumstances leading up to the killings.
Article Summary: Victims identified as Geeta Jha and her daughters Nandini, Radhika and Gauri. Their bodies were found at thier house in Govind Vatika. Police said blood at the scene appeared to have been wiped with clothes after the killings.

Article Title: Brics members favour local currency trade
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Brics finance ministers and central bank governors have recognised there cannot be a "one-size-fits-all" approach to cross-border interoperability of payment and messaging ch-annels, and backed further discussions on the issue to develop low-cost solutions.The assertion in the joint statement indicates a common payment system may have to wait as members of the bloc are seen to be in favour of local currency trade, as opposed to a common currency that was being pushed by some countries.In a statement, finance ministers and central bank governors said, "Risks to the global economic outlook remain elevated, reflecting persistent geopolitical tensions, trade fragmentation and protectionism, policy uncertainty, fiscal and inflationary pressures, growing debt and financial vulnerabilities. We continue to have serious concerns with the unilateral imposition of trade and finance-related actions, including the raising of tariffs and non-tariff measures, which distort trade and are inconsistent with WTO rules. "The statement is seen to be directed at US, which under Donald Trump has weaponised tariffs, while presidents, starting with Barack Obama, have blocked smooth functioning of WTO.Brics members have demanded that the transformation of the global economy be reflected in shareholding patterns and called for an increase in quotas in IMF, while seeking a review of the shareholding of World Bank.They underlined that voluntary financial contributions to IMF should not influence quota allocation and voting power."We also reiterate our call for improved management procedures, including through a merit-based, inclusive and transparent selection process that would increase regional diversity and representation of emerging market and developing economies in the leadership of IMF and World Bank," the statement said. While World Bank has been led by a US nominee, the IMF chief is from Europe.The bloc supported a bigger role for New Development Bank in financing development and infrastructure projects across Brics and Global South.
Article Summary: The assertion in the joint statement indicates a common payment system may have to wait. The statement is seen to be directed at US, which under Donald Trump has weaponised tariffs. Brics members have demanded that the transformation of the global economy be reflected in shareholding patterns.

Article Title: US stocks today: Wall Street inches higher as oil prices ease, inflation data calms markets
Article Text:
Wall Street inches higher as oil prices ease, inflation data calms markets

Inflation remains high, but close to expectations

Fed faces inflation and confidence concerns

US stocks moved higher on Friday as a retreat in oil prices helped ease some of the pressure on markets, and fresh inflation data came broadly in line with expectations.The S&P 500 gained 1%, putting the index on course to end a four-day losing run, its longest since June.
